issues.quote: These averages also count indirect emissions, such as from purchased electricity, so they aren't the figures CBAM counts for steel.
issues.problem: This sentence states as fact what worldsteel's averages include. The claims table marks C75 as not yet checked: it says the worldsteel method (scope 1–3) must be checked before the final lock. The script would lock with an unchecked fact in it.
issues.fix: Check the worldsteel CO₂-intensity method and record the result in claims.md. Until that is done, use: "These are the World Steel Association's averages, calculated with its own method. CBAM uses its own rules to count steel's emissions, so the two aren't the same figure."

issues.quote: Finwire reported that Stegra called its timeline for green steel unchanged
issues.problem: The source (STG2) gives the words "remains unchanged" as Finwire's reporting. The script turns them into a statement by Stegra, an operating company, without a verbatim quote. The primary press release was never read.
issues.fix: Finwire reported that the timeline for green steel "remains unchanged."

issues.quote: As of October 2026, the latest: on September 30,
issues.problem: "The latest" says nothing newer exists. The primary source (stegra.com, Cision) was not found, and the status must be checked again before publishing.
issues.fix: As of October 11, 2026, the most recent reports we found: on September 30,

issues.quote: Each tonne of carbon dioxide counted adds about eighty-two euros to the certificate bill
issues.problem: 82 € is the price for Q3 2026 only. The sentence reads as if it were a standing rate.
issues.fix: At the price for July to September 2026, each tonne of carbon dioxide counted adds about eighty-two euros to the certificate bill

issues.problem: This is a future event stated as fact without saying who set the date.
issues.fix: according to the Commission, certificate sales are scheduled to begin in February 2027

issues.quote: Arithmetically, most of that change comes from the rest of the world making far more, not from America making less.
issues.problem: C72 is the channel's own calculation (type: calc), but it isn't labelled as such.
issues.fix: By our calculation, most of that change comes from the rest of the world making far more, not from America making less.

issues.quote: Today, a government holds consent rights over some decisions along it.
issues.problem: This states the current status of an ongoing arrangement without a date. C57 deliberately avoids claiming the current status because no newer filing exists.
issues.fix: Under the terms the companies announced in June 2025, a government holds consent rights over some decisions along it.

issues.quote: under an agreement that gives an American president consent rights over certain decisions
issues.problem: This states the current terms in the present tense. The full agreement is not public, and the only source is the companies' announcement of 18/06/2025.
issues.fix: under terms that, as the two companies described them in June 2025, give an American president consent rights over certain decisions

issues.quote: Chinese steel exports hit a record one hundred thirty-one million tonnes in 2025. By weight, that's more than all the crude steel
issues.problem: The voiceover doesn't name the export basis (all steel products). Only the on-screen label shows it. The comparison holds, but the audio leaves the difference implicit.
issues.fix: Chinese exports of steel products hit a record one hundred thirty-one million tonnes in 2025. By weight, that's more than all the crude steel

issues.quote: By 1897, Carnegie wrote, that company held forty-two thousand acres of coal land
issues.problem: C16 does not say which legal entity held the land. "That company" (Frick Coke) is an inference.
issues.fix: Check the CARN passage. If it doesn't name the holder, use: "By 1897, Carnegie wrote, the holdings reached forty-two thousand acres of coal land"

issues.quote: a trial delivery is real steel, and it shows the route works
issues.problem: "Shows the route works" is an interpretation that goes beyond HYB, a single trial delivery. It isn't marked as opinion.
issues.fix: a trial delivery is real steel, and the record shows the route has produced it; on its own, it doesn't show an industry at scale.

issues.quote: so fewer suppliers can charge you for theirs
issues.problem: This explains the strategy's purpose, but no claim covers it and it isn't marked as interpretation. It also uses "you".
issues.fix: The common name for this strategy is vertical integration: owning steps of the supply chain. One explanation economists give: fewer outside suppliers can charge a margin on those steps.
